subject: Post-call: multi-path latency qualification + data boundary asks
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Tan <alice.tan@acme.com>
Cc: Ben Chu <ben.chu@acme.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: multi-path latency qualification + data boundary asks

Hi Alice / Ben — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and the concrete engineering asks so we can qualify performance and residency constraints for the POC.

Key takeaways from the call:
- Target product flows: mobile chat (interactive streaming) and batch embedding enrichment for search indexing.
- Initial P95 SLOs: interactive streaming token latency target 150–250ms p95 (frontend visible streaming increments), non-streaming completion p95 <= 400ms for 1K-token prompts.
- Throughput & concurrency: expected sustained throughput ~8K tokens/sec across the fleet with bursts to 30K tokens/sec for nightly indexing; concurrency estimate ~200 active concurrent sessions in peak.
- Regional requirement: EU data residency for EU customers, APAC low-latency routing for SEA markets, US for NA region. Failover allowed to nearest region only if data residency policy permits.
- Security: SOC2 + audit log requirement; they asked for token-level retention controls and per-customer logs.

Concrete asks (please action):
1) Please confirm whether EU-resident users must have inference executed only in EU (strict) or if pseudonymized payloads can route to other regions (soft).
2) Provide expected qps by endpoint (chat vs embeddings) and an hourly ramp plan across the first 4 weeks of POC.
3) Can Redwood provide an initial perf profile for the recommended model family at 512 seq / streaming mode (p95 CPU/GPU latencies and throughput numbers)?
4) Share any constraints on TLS termination / proxying and whether they will terminate at our edge or through their VPC.

Next steps I committed to:
- Share a draft mutual action plan and a quick streaming-latency sketch (attached).
- Internals: get perf-smoke numbers for the 7B/13B family in streaming mode and a concurrency cost estimate.

Ben / Alice, if you can answer the three asks above by EOD Friday that will unlock the POC timeline (we suggested a 2-week technical POC + 4-week validation window).

Thanks — Irene

--
Irene Choi
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123
Redwood Inference
From: Alice Tan <alice.tan@acme.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Chu <ben.chu@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 09:18:00 +0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: multi-path latency qualification + data boundary asks

Hi Irene — thanks for the clear recap. Short answers inline:

1) EU residency: strict for customer PII flows. For telemetry/metrics we can allow aggregated export, but inference on raw PII must remain in EU.
2) QPS by endpoint (initial POC week 1): chat ~120 qps (avg message tokens ~80), embeddings batch jobs scheduled nightly ~12 jobs that each submit ~200K documents (batched). Ramp plan: double chat qps each week for 3 weeks; embeddings ramp starts week 2.
3) Perf profile: we need you to propose a model variant optimized for streaming. If that includes quantized variants, please call that out and give expected speedups.
4) TLS termination: our infra team prefers TLS termination inside our VPC; we can discuss mutual TLS for control-plane APIs.

We expect to finalize legal terms next week; SOC2 evidence will be needed for procurement. I'll loop in our infra lead if we need network diagrams.

— Alice
Product Lead, AI Integrations
Acme Commerce
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Alice Tan <alice.tan@acme.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Ben Chu <ben.chu@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: multi-path latency qualification + data boundary asks

Alice — thanks, that helps. Technical follow-up and a proposed starting point from our side:

Proposed POC config (initial):
- Model: open-13B-streaming-q4 (13B quantized variant tuned for streaming). Expect ~2.5x token throughput vs fp16 at similar p95 stream-chunk latency.
- Serving mode: continuous streaming with 64-token chunking for mobile (frontend will render partial tokens).
- Batching policy: adaptive batching with per-customer concurrency cap (we recommend cap=250 for POC).
- Caching: prefix/KV cache enabled for recurring prompts; cache residency scoped per-region to respect EU residency.

SLO targets we will aim to demonstrate in POC (bench vs their traffic mix):
- Streaming token p95: <= 220ms (goal 150ms)
- Completion p95 (1K tokens): <= 380ms
- Sustained token throughput: 8–12K tokens/sec across provisioned capacity; burst headroom to 30K tokens/sec with autoscale when reserved capacity available.

Regional routing notes:
- EU-only enforcement: we will pin EU tenant to EU nodes; routing policy will drop routes that would violate strict residency (no cross-region inference).
- Failover policy: for non-PII flows, failover allowed to nearest region; for strict PII flows, failover = disabled.
- Cross-region replication: embeddings index snapshots can be copied out of EU only after explicit export approval.

Attachments: included a sketch for streaming chunking, and a mutual action plan template — Irene can tailor with dates.

Action items:
- (Aditya) Run a perf smoke (13B quantized) at 512 seq + streaming chunk and share p95 samples by EOD Thursday.
- (Irene) Share mutual action plan with concrete dates and contacts.
- (Alice) Share final decision on strict vs soft residency by Friday.

Aditya
Senior Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Chu <ben.chu@acme.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alice Tan <alice.tan@acme.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2026 09:12:00 +0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: multi-path latency qualification + data boundary asks

Irene / Aditya — quick confirmation from infra side:
- EU must be strict for inference on EU customer PII. Anything else is negotiable, but default will be strict.
- We will provide a network diagram and a contact in our security team for SOC2 evidence collection next week.
- For TLS we will terminate in our VPC; we want a short runbook for how Redwood handles mTLS for the control plane.

Thanks, looking forward to the perf numbers — if your p95 streaming numbers are in the ballpark we can lock the POC start on 2026-06-08.

Ben
Infrastructure Lead, Acme Commerce
